author: Vincent Chow
description:
The United States announced sanctions on a Hong Kong company on Friday for allegedly helping launder funds for a sanctioned Iranian exchange house, the latest Chinese entity to be targeted as part of Washington’s expanded efforts to squeeze Iran’s financial sector.
The development comes as Washington has in recent days slapped new Iran-related sanctions on various Chinese entities, prompting Beijing to vow retaliation just weeks before Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the...
title: US Treasury sanctions Hong Kong-based firm over Iran money laundering ties

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
On the windswept plains just south of Tibet’s second-largest city, the towering smart inspection systems and automated cargo gantries of a brand-new international land port gleam under the plateau’s high-altitude sun.
Official road maps predict the multibillion-yuan project in Shigatse will process up to 300 trucks daily by the end of 2030 – loading cargo off trains and onto the trucks that will take goods to their final destination. It will also allow the authorities to carry out customs checks...
title: Can Beijing’s gateway plan for Tibet survive geopolitics and natural disasters?

author: Shouqing Zhu
description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) poses risks that do not respect national borders, from cyberattacks and misinformation to system malfunction and potentially dangerous misuse. In a geopolitically charged world, does greater incompatibility between countries make AI safer?
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres offered a clear answer at the inaugural UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance: “When countries align on how to test systems, measure risk and assign responsibility, safety travels with the...
title: US-China AI rivalry needn’t preclude cooperation

author: Chao Kong
description:
“Asia’s water tower” is heading towards a more unpredictable and unstable future, according to a new study measuring the Tibetan Plateau’s stability.
The study, published on August 21 in Nature Communications, examined the entropy of the region to gauge how much chaos or disorder was building up in a complex system.
The results were released just days before a catastrophic flash flood struck the Nepal-China border, killing hundreds and leaving a trail of devastation along the way.
Chen Xiaosong,...
title: The ‘Asian water tower’ is starting to wobble, computer simulations show

author: Fan Chen
description:
Beijing has formally removed former senior officers Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli as members of China’s supreme military command.
The two generals have been under investigation for alleged discipline violations since January and were officially stripped of their positions on the Central Military Commission (CMC) at a meeting of the National People’s Congress’ Standing Committee on Friday.
As the CMC’s senior vice-chairman, Zhang was the highest-ranking uniformed officer in the Chinese military....
title: China strips former generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli of top military positions

author: Nayan Seth,Khushboo Razdan
description:
The Central Asian country of Uzbekistan has approached the United States about joining Pax Silica, Washington’s flagship initiative on artificial intelligence (AI) supply chains, a month after signing up for China’s own global grouping, the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (Waico).
Uzbekistan’s ambassador to the US, Furqat Sidikov, said Tashkent had formally notified the US State Department in a diplomatic note last week requesting to join the US-led initiative.
“Now, the...
title: Uzbekistan tests US-China AI rift with bid to join rival tech bloc

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Within hours of a devastating glacier collapse on the China-Nepal border, a Beijing-based satellite company had already redirected six of its satellites to survey the disaster zone.
The high-resolution radar images they captured revealed a massive collapse site near a remote mountain pass.
Unlike optical sensors, radar signals can pierce through haze and cloud, mapping terrain changes with high precision even in the rugged Himalayan plateau.

The swift commercial response also underscores a...
title: China’s radar satellites capture sharp images of glacier collapse site in Nepal

author: Bao Yinan
description:
With the end of the 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding, tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have flared again. The crisis in the strait highlights how the security and stability of key international waterways are becoming an increasingly urgent global concern.
Over the past decade, major maritime routes have been affected by regional armed conflicts, geopolitical tensions and growing security risks. These disruptions have exposed a vulnerability in the global trading system: a key...
title: US and China must team up to keep maritime trade routes free and safe

author: Ling Xin
description:
Gong Zizheng, a pioneer of space debris research and a key figure in China’s planned asteroid defence mission, has died at 61.
A top government adviser and prominent leader in international space debris organisations, Gong died on Saturday after a battle with illness, according to Chinese media reports. No further details were given.
On social media, one of Gong’s colleagues at the China Academy of Space Technology remembered him as a prolific scientist deeply devoted to his work, a warm and...
title: Gong Zizheng, who led China’s planetary defence project, dies at 61

author: Victoria Bela
description:
To scientists, the cause of this week’s deadly flash flood on the border between China and Nepal is clear: a glacier high on the Nepal side of the Himalayan range collapsed, sending catastrophic amounts of water and debris downstream.
Initial uncertainty over the cause of the event fuelled a wave of misinformation on social media, some of which pinned the blame for the event on Chinese-built infrastructure in the region.
But a war of information over China’s activities in the region continued to...
title: How the Nepal flash flood unleashed a wave of anti-China misinformation

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
This week’s devastating floods on the China-Nepal border could be a catalyst for joint early-warning systems, particularly in relation to a proposed rail link between the countries.
Rescuers were still struggling on Thursday to reach Gyirong Port in the Tibet autonomous region where a mudslide struck a day earlier, following flash floods from Nepal.
The port is the region’s main foreign trade gateway, which handles a third of China’s trade with its neighbour. Gyirong is also one end of a...
title: Could the China-Nepal disaster spur a safety rethink for a flagship rail project?

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping may take a business delegation to Washington next month, when he is also likely to sign a trade-war truce extension with US President Donald Trump.
The potential business delegation is under negotiation ahead of the September 24 summit, the South China Morning Post reported, citing four people with knowledge of the matter. US executives, including Apple’s Tim Cook and Tesla’s Elon Musk, accompanied Trump on his state visit to China in May.
Both countries want to...
title: Xi-Trump summit plans, Nepal disaster, SCO summit

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Bangladesh has for the first time confirmed a long-expected deal to purchase China’s 4.5-generation J-10CE fighters, pointing to the jet’s combat performance against Rafale fighters in last year’s India-Pakistan conflict.
One military expert said it was a sign that the global perception of Chinese weapons was shifting and the market would gradually open.
Zahed Ur Rahman, information and broadcasting adviser to the prime minister of Bangladesh, told journalists on Tuesday that a draft proposal to...
title: Bangladesh confirms Chinese J-10CE jet deal, citing Rafale kill in India-Pakistan clash

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Beijing has promised to send emergency aid to Nepal as Chinese rescuers continued to fight their way through hazardous conditions in an effort to reach the border checkpoint hit by deadly flash floods this week.
The disaster has left five dead and 558 missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county, while Nepal reported 469 dead and nearly 1,000 missing.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has sent a message of condolence to his Nepalese counterpart Ram Chandra Poudel following the devastating mudslides, state...
title: China pledges to send urgent emergency aid to Nepal after deadly landslide

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
A peace plan agreed between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Rwanda-backed M23 movement last weekend could open the rebel-held Rubaya coltan deposit and other parts of mineral-rich eastern Congo to US investors.
But observers say that even a lasting settlement would leave the United States far behind China, whose companies have spent decades building mining assets, relationships and supply chains across the country.
The peace road map followed five days of talks and set out steps and...
title: Truce in DR Congo offers US mining foothold while Chinese firms dominate output

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Australia’s decision to axe partnerships with two Chinese universities has raised concerns that Canberra is moving to align with Washington on research security policy.
The decision came after the United States expanded its restrictions on research entities from China.
One analyst warned that Canberra’s latest move would not hinder Chinese progress, but it could leave Australia locked out of top-tier scientific research.
The Australian National University confirmed in a statement that it would...
title: Will Australia be locked out of top scientific research by shunning Chinese universities?

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Typhoon Saudel made landfall in the eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, disrupting flights and ferry services across major urban centres, including the industrial hub of Ningbo and the economic powerhouse of Shanghai.
Ningbo Lishe International Airport suspended all flight operations from 11.30pm on Thursday. Even though services resumed at 11am on Friday, some 16 inbound and 28 outbound flights were cancelled for the day.
In the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou, a base for private enterprise, 197...
title: Storm travel chaos as Typhoon Saudel makes double landfall in China

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. The path to America is narrowing. Here’s what that means for legal immigrants
US green card interviews are on hold worldwide, student and work visas are subject to new restrictions, and citizenship is under fresh scrutiny. The SCMP...
title: US visa interviews on hold; China slams fresh sanctions over Iran: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The record heat and extreme weather seen across East Asia this summer have prompted warnings that climate change will be an increasing challenge for military planners focused on potential flashpoints such as the Taiwan Strait.
Besides the risks to both troops and equipment, typhoons and other storms could also damage critical infrastructure and disrupt training, as well as divert personnel and resources towards emergency relief.
Although militaries may be able to adapt in peacetime, they may...
title: How typhoons and extreme weather could undermine Taiwan Strait combat readiness

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The death toll from catastrophic flash floods and mudslides at the Gyirong Port border crossing between China and Nepal continued to rise on Friday, as satellite images revealed the full scale of the destruction.
As of Friday morning, three people were confirmed dead and 558 missing on the Chinese side of the border, with 469 dead and at least 644 missing in Nepal.

The tragedy unfolded on Wednesday morning when a massive Himalayan landslide triggered a fast-moving debris flow that swept down...
title: China-Nepal disaster death toll nears 500 as lake overflow threatens rescue work

author: Julie Zhang
description:
Chinese surgeons last month completed the world’s first commercial surgery to implant an invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) device in a patient with a spinal cord injury, a milestone in the neurotechnology development race with US companies like Elon Musk’s Neuralink.
This month a Chinese company, state-owned PICC Property and Casualty, launched the world’s first commercial insurance policy covering BCI implantation surgery. September will see the first undergraduates in China to major in...
title: China thinks big on brain-computer interfaces after world-first surgery

author: Josephine Ma
description:
Trita Parsi is co-founder and executive vice-president of the Quincy Institute, a Washington-based think tank. He is an expert on US-Iranian relations, Iranian foreign policy and the geopolitics of the Middle East. He has written four books on US foreign policy in the Middle East, with a particular focus on Iran and Israel. Born in Iran, Parsi moved to Sweden with his family as a child and then to the United States as an adult.
SCMP Plus readers get early access to articles in the Open Questions...
title: Iran expert on China’s balancing act amid conflict with US and Israel

author: Yuanyue Dang,William Zheng
description:
The South China Morning Post has launched a major data project diving into President Xi Jinping’s signature anti-graft campaign. In the fourth part of an accompanying series, Yuanyue Dang and William Zheng delve into the broader reach of the campaign.
While economic crimes are often seen as the target of President Xi Jinping’s crusade against corruption, the campaign has become much wider.
Thirteen years since it began, it is now increasingly about how officials use their power, whether they toe...
title: Xi’s crusade against corruption has gone well beyond economic crime

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
US green card interviews are on hold worldwide, student and work visas are subject to new restrictions, and citizenship is under fresh scrutiny. Here’s what the latest US immigration crackdown means for people planning to study, work or settle in America.
Why did the US cancel immigrant visa interviews?
US embassies and consulates around the world have postponed immigrant visa interviews so that officers can train on a stricter “public charge” test: whether an applicant is likely to rely on...
title: The path to America is narrowing. Here’s what that means for legal immigrants
